sources.title: Doodleberry feature map
sources.used_for: Status of partial features and which WP owns each open row

capabilities.capability: System requirements and installation: the supported OS, GPU and tablet setup, and a one-step install.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios image every workstation the same way so files open and render identically.

match.note: engine.doctor checks core, audio and tool dependencies and prints the exact fix for each (tools/setup.sh applies them); engine.info reports the renderers available.

capabilities.capability: Getting-started projects and startup content: ready-made documents and sample characters to start from.
capabilities.pro_use: Teams start a new episode from a house template rather than an empty canvas.

match.note: film.create makes an empty film folder. film.from_template builds a storyboard from a format template (dialogue, explainer, myth_vs_data).

capabilities.capability: A custom content folder that holds user brushes, scripts, styles and presets in one place.
capabilities.pro_use: A studio keeps its own brushes, rigs and tools in one place, version-controlled and shared by everyone.

match.note: Characters, clip libraries and third-party assets are files in the repo, and every asset has a manifest row with its licence.

capabilities.capability: Licence activation, deactivation and automatic update checks.
capabilities.pro_use: IT moves seats between machines and controls which version is in use.

match.note: Doodleberry is in-house code with no seats or activation. The version is whatever git checkout is in use.

capabilities.capability: Live Performance Mode (14.5): drive a rig in real time from a webcam, microphone, keyboard or game controller, on top of existing animation.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for fast dialogue blocking, live streams and VTuber-style shows with a studio character.

match.note: actout.clip turns a recorded take (MediaPipe body and face) into a clip. Real-time live tracking (E9) is a WP-12 follow-on.

capabilities.capability: Live Playback capture: keep a performance as editable keyframes, with separate passes per character or per selected layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators capture a rough take and then polish the keys by hand, layering several passes.

match.note: A take becomes a reduced-key clip on the character, and timeline.edit moves or resizes it. Multi-person takes and live passes are in WP-12.

capabilities.capability: Face-tracked head turns and expressions: tracking drives a head-turn control bone and facial Smart Bones, including eyes, brows and mouth.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives quick, natural head and face acting for talking-head and dialogue scenes.

match.note: Face Landmarker blendshapes already become eye, brow, gaze and mouth keys. Feeding head yaw into the puppet's turn control is named in WP-12.

capabilities.capability: Gamepad and joystick controls: buttons trigger actions and sticks move bones, optionally holding the pose on release.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets a puppeteer trigger gestures and expressions live, like playing an instrument.

match.note: There is no live input device path. It fits WP-12's live tracking follow-on.

capabilities.capability: Virtual webcam output: broadcast the live-performed character to meeting or streaming software.
capabilities.pro_use: Puts a branded character into live calls, classes and streams.

match.note: Live 2D avatars of the cast (E9) are a WP-12 P2 follow-on.

capabilities.capability: Licence types (Pro vs Debut, perpetual, floating or network licences for studios).
capabilities.pro_use: Studios use floating licences so seats follow the artist.

match.note: Doodleberry is in-house code with no product licensing. The licences of components it uses are tracked separately (licence.ledger).

capabilities.capability: The end-user licence agreement, which sets how the software and the bundled content may be used.
capabilities.pro_use: Legal checks whether the bundled content may appear in client or broadcast work.

match.note: Doodleberry has no EULA. The matching control is a licence class for every component, with restricted inputs flagged at the posting gate. WP-33 finishes per-render recording.

capabilities.capability: Bezier curve editing: add points, then shape curvature with full handles or smooth and peaked corners.
capabilities.pro_use: Cleans character outlines precisely so they deform well under bones.

match.note: Parts are SVG path data, so they can be edited through a layered-SVG round trip (for example in Inkscape). There is no in-house handle editor. Vector editing is a WP-34 integration candidate.

capabilities.capability: Freehand drawing with pressure, smoothing, auto-fill, Shift for straight lines, trimming of stray tails and welding of endpoints (14.0, 14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Used for rough-to-clean drawing straight into the rig, and for frame-by-frame effects.

match.note: The Rig Canvas ink uses perfect-freehand pressure and RDP simplification, and puppet.save writes the result. A stabiliser, tail trimming and welding are in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Boolean shape operations: add, subtract and intersect shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: Builds complex props and cut-outs (holes, highlights) quickly.

match.note: Only even-odd fill rules exist (strokes 'rule': 'evenodd'). Shape booleans belong with the Rig Canvas tools in WP-18. Skia-pathops or Clipper2 are already used for toon shading.

capabilities.capability: Point selection and transformation: lasso or box select, then move, scale and rotate about a pivot.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to adjust a mouth or a hand drawing without redrawing it.

match.note: The feature map lists lasso and transform under WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Shape primitives (rectangle, oval, star, arrow) and the blob brush for filled organic shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives fast blocking of props, backgrounds and filled masses.

match.note: Ink strokes are already filled outline shapes (blob-like). There are no primitives in the Rig Canvas. Sets and props are drawn in code (sets/*.js).

capabilities.capability: An eraser that removes both fills and strokes, optionally limited to the selected shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to fix drawings in place.

match.note: The eraser is in the feature map's brush-engine row, owned by WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Point reduction: simplify a curve to fewer points.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps rigged art light so it deforms cleanly and renders fast.

match.note: Strokes are RDP-simplified on capture. Cleaning up imported parts (picosvg, svgo, vpype) is in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Scatter brush: stamp many varied copies of a shape (leaves, grass, crowds of dots).
capabilities.pro_use: Used to dress backgrounds quickly.

match.note: proc.cook scatters points (seeded, minimum spacing) and instances cast members or 3D blocks on them.

capabilities.capability: Point deformers: perspective, shear and bend applied to selected points.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to fake a turn or a foreshortening on a drawing without redrawing it.

match.note: WP-34 covers vector editing and deformers through Synfig core and Inkscape.

capabilities.capability: Noise tool and vector noise: random wobble on points, optionally animated, or only while the shape moves.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives a hand-made, jittery line look.

match.note: Deterministic line boil (cycled displacement fields at a chosen fps, amount and frequency) gives the animated-wobble look. A permanent jitter of points is not offered.

capabilities.capability: Magnet tool: drag points with a soft falloff, and Shift-drag back toward their frame-0 shape (14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Used to sculpt squash, cheeks and cloth on a frame.

match.note: There is no point-level sculpting in the Rig Canvas.

capabilities.capability: Liquid shapes (14.0): soft vector shapes that merge, subtract and intersect live as they animate.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for fire, smoke, water and blobby character effects.

match.note: This needs live vector booleans in the engine (WP-34 vector editing). The effects use (fire, water, smoke) also overlaps WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Create shapes and paint-bucket fills from linework, with gap closing, a trace mode that outlines visible regions across layers, and weld-crossings (14.3, 14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Colours line art quickly, including rough lines that do not quite close.

match.note: The Rig Canvas bucket fills an inked area, closes gaps up to about 10 px and tucks the fill under the ink. Trace-across-layers is in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Recolour mode: change an existing shape's fill or stroke colour without new points.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for colour passes and palette changes late in production.

match.note: Fills and strokes name palette slots, so recolouring a slot recolours every shape using it. set_opts recolours sets.

capabilities.capability: Line width per point, with pressure, random width and whole-curve resizing.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives an expressive inked line weight that tapers at joints.

match.note: Each stroke has one width, and Rig Canvas ink bakes pressure into its outline. Animatable per-point width belongs with line styles in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Hide edge: make chosen segments of an outline invisible while the fill stays.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives seamless joins where parts overlap, such as the neck or shoulders.

match.note: A stroke can drop its stroke colour entirely, but not per segment. Artists draw parts past the joint instead (puppet.coach checks this).

capabilities.capability: Stroke exposure: animate a line drawing itself on or off.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for write-on titles, signatures and diagram reveals.

match.note: There is no draw-on for vector strokes (only typed consoles and procedural growth such as the roots kit). It should join WP-15 with kinetic typography.

capabilities.capability: Curve profile: shape a stroke's cross-section along its length, animatable with an offset (14.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Used for ribbon-like hair, tubes and stylised outlines.

match.note: It should join WP-15 (line styles and medium simulation for vector lines).

capabilities.capability: Point colours: colour that varies across a shape, following its curve.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives soft colour transitions on vector characters without gradients.

match.note: It should join WP-15. Every renderer would need it (WP-14).

capabilities.capability: Brush opacity and colour drift per point, driven by pressure or randomness and animatable (14.3).
capabilities.pro_use: Gives natural-media lines (pencil, watercolour) on rigged vector art.

match.note: Brush engines are a WP-34 integration candidate (Krita, libmypaint). The vector medium look is also in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Build a bone hierarchy: add, select, reparent and offset bones, set pivots and pose with forward kinematics.
capabilities.pro_use: This is the base of every cut-out rig.

match.note: Each part is a bone with a parent and a pivot, posed by angles relative to the drawn pose. The Rig Canvas sets pivots, and doodle.cut confirms them for doodles.

capabilities.capability: Inverse kinematics while posing: drag a hand or foot and the chain follows, with bone locks and targets.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives fast posing and planted feet for walks.

match.note: There is two-bone IK with foot pins, and N-bone FABRIK chains. The Rig Canvas Pose tool drags hands and feet by IK.

capabilities.capability: Bone strength and region binding: each bone's falloff weights nearby points for smooth deformation.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives smooth elbows, knees and torsos without visible hinges.

match.note: Mesh strokes with per-vertex weights (puppet v0.5) and bendy limbs exist, but only in the SVG renderer (bendy limbs also in Grease Pencil). Other renderers are in WP-14. There is no strength-painting tool.

capabilities.capability: Sketch bones: draw a whole chain of bones in one gesture.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives quick rigging of tails, hair and props.

match.note: Rigs are made automatically (pivots estimated on import, suggested for doodles, generated for cast.generate). Interactive chain drawing in the Rig Canvas is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Bind layers and bind points: attach whole drawings or individual points to chosen bones.
capabilities.pro_use: Controls exactly which art follows which bone.

match.note: A part's strokes move with its bone, and swap sets anchor to a part. Per-vertex binding exists only for mesh strokes.

capabilities.capability: Bone physics: pill-shaped collision regions, motors (speed and torque), and lock tip, inside a physics group.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for ragdolls, machines and objects that tumble.

match.note: Rigid bodies (balls, boxes, props) collide with each other and with static colliders in physics.solve (deterministic Rapier). Physical bones (ragdolls, motors) are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Smart Bones: a bone's rotation automatically drives corrective actions (point shapes, colours, switches, order, flips), one action per direction.
capabilities.pro_use: This is Moho's signature technique: clean elbows and head turns, and face rigs driven by one dial.

match.note: Controls (v0.4 driven keys) drive angles, shifts, swaps, z and scale from one value, and swaps can follow a part's angle (v0.9 by_angle); corrective point shapes driven by a bone's angle are WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Control bones as dials or levers that a rig exposes for expressions and turns, including 360-degree Smart Bones (14.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Animators work from a small set of high-level controls instead of many bones.

match.note: Named controls with a range (for example Pip's 'turn') are animated per shot as [[t, value]]. Wrap-around 360 controls are not offered.

capabilities.capability: Force / wind tool (13.5): wind with strength, direction and turbulence acting on dynamic bones.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for hair, flags, grass and clothes in outdoor scenes.

match.note: physics.solve has gravity and kicks but no wind field; wind acting on springs and dynamic parts is WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Vitruvian bones (13.5): one bone layer holds several alternate bone sets and drawings (for example front and side limbs), switched per frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives foreshortening, turnarounds and extreme poses in a single rig.

match.note: Views override parts, pivots and swaps per view and are switched by the timeline with a turn smear. Every renderer and exporter supports them.

capabilities.capability: Bone constraints: angle limits, point-at targets (now reaching a full 360 degrees), copy and independent targeting, and ignoring IK.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps rigs from breaking and automates eye aim and props.

match.note: Joint limits, look-at with time windows, IK/FK blending, IK targets on other characters, stretchy IK and copy-rotation constraints exist.

capabilities.capability: Animated bone parenting and parent switching over time.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for hand-offs, picking things up, and a character mounting a vehicle.

match.note: Props switch parents (hand to hand, throws, drops); characters reach for each other's parts (interact.solve handshakes: an IK target on another character, blended in and out). Re-parenting a character's own parts over time is WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Transform layers (move, scale, rotate) and set a layer's origin, all animatable.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to place and move characters and props within a scene.

match.note: Characters are placed per shot and travel over time. Props have positions, spin and travel.

capabilities.capability: Follow path: a layer travels along a drawn curve, optionally oriented to it.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for flights, vehicles and characters walking a curved route.

match.note: Characters walk along drawn curves (place.path) and props follow paths (props path, oriented to the curve when asked).

capabilities.capability: Rotate a layer about X or Y (3D tilt of flat art) and shear a layer.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives cheap perspective on signs, doors and cards.

match.note: Flat layers in depth and the multiplane camera are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Insert text as an editable layer with font, size and colour.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for titles, signs and labels inside the scene.

match.note: Text and sign overlays and title kit elements are timed per shot. Sinhala and other scripts fall back per glyph.

capabilities.capability: Word balloons: speech balloons with tails pointing at a speaker.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for comic-style dialogue and captioned, sound-off cuts.

match.note: Say, shout and whisper bubbles are synced to the voice and avoid collisions. Thought clouds and narration boxes are WP-17.

capabilities.capability: Layer selector and eyedropper: pick a layer or copy a style by clicking on the canvas.
capabilities.pro_use: Speeds up hands-on editing in dense scenes.

match.note: In Doodleberry, parts, cast and colours are named ids and palette slots that agents address directly. The Rig Canvas already selects parts by clicking.

capabilities.capability: Track (pan) and zoom the camera, keyframed.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for push-ins, reveals and following action.

match.note: Camera keys [[t, [cx, cy, zoom]]] are folded into the bake for every renderer. camera_auto adds speaker framing and punch-ins as a pure function of time.

capabilities.capability: Roll the camera (tilt the frame sideways).
capabilities.pro_use: Used for dutch angles and impact moments.

match.note: Camera keys have no rotation. It should join WP-36 (multiplane camera).

capabilities.capability: Pan/tilt the camera in 3D among layers placed at depth, giving real parallax.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives multiplane-style depth in backgrounds.

match.note: Some sets fake parallax (forest depths). True multiplane depth is WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Show the camera's motion path, and orbit the workspace to view the scene from outside the camera.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to check and plan complex camera moves.

match.note: A camera-keys lane in the Studio timeline is in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Workspace navigation: pan, zoom, rotate and flip the canvas view (not the output).
capabilities.pro_use: Lets the artist draw at a comfortable angle and check a drawing mirrored.

match.note: This is a view-only editor convenience. Doodleberry renders straight from data, and the Rig Canvas has its own canvas view.

capabilities.capability: Switch layers: a set of alternative drawings, one shown at a time and keyed on the timeline (mouths, hands, eyes).
capabilities.pro_use: Used for lip-sync charts, hand poses and expression swaps.

match.note: Mouths, eyes, brows, pupils and hand poses are swap sets, chosen by lip-sync, blink or name.

capabilities.capability: Particle layers: emit copies of child layers with speed, spread, lifetime and gravity.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for rain, snow, sparks, smoke and simple crowds.

match.note: Particles (confetti, snow, rain) and procedural crowds of cast members exist; emitting copies of arbitrary child layers is WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Image masking and cropping: cut away part of a bitmap with a vector mask.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to split painted or scanned art into riggable pieces.

match.note: Raster parts are cut by polygons with hidden overlap seams. General per-layer masks are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Video tracking (much improved in 14.5): track a feature through footage or image sequences, with a second point for angle and scale, and apply it to a layer as keys.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to pin animation onto live-action plates or to follow a moving camera.

match.note: actout.clip tracks people only. Tracking points and backgrounds (camera-motion compensation) is in WP-12.

capabilities.capability: Face tracking from video (14.5): analyse recorded footage into facial bones, facial Smart Bones and a face mesh.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives quick facial performance capture for dialogue.

match.note: A recorded take gives eye, brow, gaze and mouth keys on an existing rig. Head yaw into the turn control is WP-12. Building a rig from the face is not planned.

capabilities.capability: A working area that previews close to the final render (the 14.0 graphics engine), with display-quality toggles for effects, masks and brushes.
capabilities.pro_use: Animators judge the final look while they work, without test renders.

match.note: The player page is the SVG renderer itself (each frame a pure function of time), so the preview matches the render exactly.

capabilities.capability: Playback controls: play, loop, step frames and jump between keys.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for timing reviews.

match.note: The Studio timeline and the review room scrub and frame-step. export.web gives a standalone player with play, scrub and frame step.

capabilities.capability: Toolbar, status bar, docking windows and the Pro split views (side by side, four way).
capabilities.pro_use: Lets each artist arrange the screen to suit them.

match.note: Doodleberry is agent-native: tools are commands (engine.commands lists them with schemas) rather than a docked GUI.

capabilities.capability: A layer list with nesting, reordering, visibility and quick settings.
capabilities.pro_use: Organises a character and a scene into a manageable tree.

match.note: Draw order is z per part (switchable by controls and clips). Scene order comes from the cast list.

capabilities.capability: Searching and filtering the layer list, including showing only animated layers (14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Finds what is keyed in big rigs.

match.note: timeline.get returns, per cast member, every clip layer, emotion and gaze key. The film data is plain JSON that agents can search.

capabilities.capability: Layer comps: saved sets of visible layers that can be rendered separately (for example characters only, or background only).
capabilities.pro_use: Used for render passes handed to compositing.

match.note: The Synfig and Grease Pencil renderers already draw characters on alpha over a separate set video, and Lottie can drop the background. Named multi-pass output (OpenEXR passes) is WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Layer referencing: instances of a layer or character that update from a master, including from other files.
capabilities.pro_use: One character master is used across many scenes and episodes.

match.note: Films reference puppets from the cast library by name, so a fix to the master reaches every film on its next render.

capabilities.capability: Layer colours and tags for organisation.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives visual grouping in large scenes.

match.note: This is a GUI organisation aid. Doodleberry's data is named ids.

capabilities.capability: Vector layers: resolution-independent drawings made of points, curves and shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: The default art type for rigged characters.

match.note: Parts are SVG path data in artboard units, so output is resolution independent.

capabilities.capability: Image layers: bitmaps (including painted or photographed art) placed and rigged like vectors.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for painted characters and scanned art.

match.note: These make raster parts (puppet v0.3) from PSD or ORA layers, photos or scans. Raster parts render only in SVG. Other renderers are WP-14.

capabilities.capability: Image sequence layers: a numbered sequence or video played as one layer.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for hand-drawn effects, rotoscope plates and pre-rendered elements.

match.note: Drawn levels (a sequence of drawings with exposures) are WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Group layers, with group-level masking and shared settings.
capabilities.pro_use: Masks a character's clothing patterns or shading inside a group.

match.note: The part hierarchy groups art. Group masks are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Bone layers that carry the skeleton for their children.
capabilities.pro_use: The container for every rig.

match.note: The skeleton lives in the puppet file. All renderers read the baked animation from tools/bake.mjs.

capabilities.capability: Interpolated switch layers: smooth morphs between switch drawings that share point counts.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives smooth mouth and hand transitions instead of pops.

match.note: Swaps are discrete (the only exception is a squash smear on view changes). Morphs between drawings or views are in WP-43.

capabilities.capability: Frame-by-frame layers: traditional hand-drawn animation inside a rigged scene.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for effects, smears and hand-drawn moments mixed with the rig.

match.note: Hand-drawn animation with drawn levels and an X-sheet is WP-35.

capabilities.capability: Note layers: sticky notes placed in the scene for collaborators.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for director or supervisor notes on specific shots.

match.note: Notes are pinned to frames in review.json, and review.fix turns them into checked data edits.

capabilities.capability: Audio layers: several sound files placed on the timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for dialogue, music and effects tracks lined up to picture.

match.note: Voice, a procedural score and timed cues are mixed with stems. Waveform lanes and moving, trimming or replacing audio clips are WP-40.

capabilities.capability: 3D layers: imported 3D models (OBJ) or 2D shapes converted to 3D, in the scene.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for 3D props and sets under a 2D camera.

match.note: A three.js GLB renderer exists as a tool (tools/three/run3d.mjs), but no film command composites it with 2D. Blender 3D sets and passes are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Patch layers: a masked copy that hides the seam where two overlapping parts meet.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives clean shoulders, hips and necks on cut-out rigs.

match.note: Ink cuts keep hidden overlaps, puppet.coach measures gaps opened by bending, and layer order can be keyed per pose (v0.9) to swap layering at joints; masked patch copies are WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Text layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for on-screen text that stays editable.

match.note: This is the same match as moho-layer-tools-4.

capabilities.capability: Layer shadows, shading and outlines (drop shadow, inner shading, outline), previewed live.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives a lit, finished look on flat art without extra drawing.

match.note: Cel-shadow bands and rim light work in SVG, and ground shadows are on by default. Other renderers are WP-14. General layer effects are WP-36. Note that drop shadows are flagged by the AI-look lint.

capabilities.capability: Motion blur (realistic, Pro) on moving layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Smooths fast action.

match.note: Sub-frame motion blur on fast shots only is in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Masking modes per layer (add, subtract, clip, exclude strokes).
capabilities.pro_use: Used for clothing patterns, eye whites clipping pupils, and shading inside shapes.

match.note: This is in the compositor: masks and mattes.

capabilities.capability: Blend modes (multiply, screen, add, Color Burn, Linear Dodge) that match PSD behaviour (14.1, 14.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Gives lighting passes and faithful round trips with Photoshop art.

match.note: Only ffmpeg overlays exist. Blend modes are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Animatable layer opacity, blur and pixelation (14.1, 14.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Used for fades, focus pulls and stylised effects.

match.note: Stroke opacity is static, and finishing presets (grade, vignette, grain) apply per shot. Animated layer opacity and blur are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Depth sort and depth shift: order layers by their distance from the camera.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives correct layering when characters walk in depth.

match.note: Z order is per part and switchable by controls and clips (SVG and Grease Pencil only). Depth planes are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Line boil and smart line boil: redraw jitter at set intervals, optionally only while the shape moves (14.0, 14.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Gives a hand-drawn shimmer on rigged art.

match.note: Deterministic boil (fps, amount, frequency) exists on characters, bubbles and signs. Boil only during motion is new and should join WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Particles tab: count, speed, spread, lifetime, emission along curves, per-particle offsets and emission order (14.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Used to tune effects and procedural hair or tails.

match.note: Count, speed spread, start and seed per particle preset; emission along curves and per-particle lifetimes are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: 3D options: extrude or lathe a vector shape into a 3D object.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for quick 3D props from 2D drawings.

match.note: 3D props through Blender are in WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Physics tab: rigid bodies with mass, friction, bounciness and collisions between layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for falling objects, stacks and collisions without hand keys.

match.note: Bodies with density, friction and restitution collide with each other and with static colliders (deterministic Rapier), baked into prop tracks; contacts can be retimed onto the beat.

capabilities.capability: Shared named styles applied to many shapes, so one change updates all of them, including bulk edits of a character's line width, brush and boil (14.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps colour and line consistent across a character and an episode.

match.note: Palette slots share colour across all shapes. Shared line styles (width, brush) across a character belong with line styles in WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Gradient and texture fills.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives soft shading and patterned clothing.

match.note: Puppet strokes take flat palette colours only (sets drawn in code may use gradients). It should join WP-18 for authoring, with WP-14 for renderer parity.

capabilities.capability: Brushes and freehand styles (wet ink, charcoal, gouache, watercolour, pencil), with brush folders.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives natural-media looks on vector rigs.

match.note: Medium simulation for vector lines (pencil, marker, crayon) and a watercolour pass are in WP-15. Brush engines are WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Swatches and a colour palette library.
capabilities.pro_use: Holds show palettes and colour models.

match.note: Named palette slots per puppet. The brand kit palette is measured by brand.check.

capabilities.capability: A library of reusable characters, props, scenes and actions, with tabs and search.
capabilities.pro_use: Teams reuse a show's cast and props from one place.

match.note: This is the cast library with provenance. Clips come from template libraries and character clips. Sets come from sets/*.js.

capabilities.capability: A details panel with item metadata.
capabilities.pro_use: Shows who made an asset and how it may be used.

match.note: Lists author, licence and voice profile, and checks every third-party file has a licence row.

capabilities.capability: Library locations for teams (shared folders that several artists use).
capabilities.pro_use: Gives a shared studio asset store.

match.note: The library is in git and new characters merge through prod.merge. Assignments and locks on characters are WP-39.

capabilities.capability: Bought or downloaded content packs added to the library.
capabilities.pro_use: Speeds up production with stock assets.

match.note: Third-party assets are licence-tracked. More packs (Kenney, Open Peeps, Humaaans) are WP-16. Downloaded packs are never committed.

capabilities.capability: Parametric character generation (body, face, clothing and style tabs) into a ready rig.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives fast background cast and prototypes.

match.note: Builds an original rigged humanoid from build, age, skin, hair, outfit and accessories. It works with every clip and renderer.

capabilities.capability: Walk-cycle designer: parametric walks with stride and style, and making the character walk across the scene.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives quick locomotion for crowds and blocking.

match.note: interact.solve walks a character along a curved path with the stride matched to the clip and feet planted (measured under 1 px of slide); a parametric walk designer (stride, bounce, style) is WP-11.

capabilities.capability: Rotating the generated character through 360 degrees.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives turnarounds without redrawing.

match.note: Generated characters get a turn control (three-quarter head), and views can be drawn. Turnaround boards are WP-18. Morphs between views are WP-43.

capabilities.capability: Designing your own actions that work on any wizard character.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets a whole cast share one motion set.

match.note: Clips are defined per template, so every character on a template plays them.

capabilities.capability: Creating new content (hair, outfits, parts) for the wizard.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets a studio extend the generator with its own style.

match.note: Generator options are fixed in code. Outfits as swap sets and a family look as parameters are WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Keyframes per animation channel: add, select, move, copy and delete, including editing switch-type keys.
capabilities.pro_use: This is the core of keyframe animation.

match.note: The timeline edits clip layers (move, resize, add, delete). Per-joint keys are recorded in the Rig Canvas and saved as clips. Dragging lines and shots, and a keys lane, are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Interpolation methods per key: smooth, linear, ease in/out, step, cycle, noisy, bounce, elastic, stagger.
capabilities.pro_use: Shapes the timing feel of each move.

match.note: Keys ease by smoothstep. There is stepped timing, looping clips, and anticipation and overshoot as a filter. Per-key interpolation types and curves are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Motion graph: edit animation curves directly.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives fine spacing and polish.

match.note: The curve (graph) editor is in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Onion skins: ghosts of nearby frames or keys, coloured and movable (14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Essential for spacing and frame-by-frame work.

match.note: Onion skins are in WP-35, with expression boards with onion skin in WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Animation interval: animate on twos or threes.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives a hand-made, limited-animation feel.

match.note: Animate on 12s, 8s or 6s per shot while the film runs at 30 fps. Repeated frames are deduplicated at render.

capabilities.capability: Timeline markers: named or interval markers for beats and notes.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets animators time to music and dialogue beats.

match.note: There is a beat grid from the score, plus dialogue lanes with word ticks, and times anchor to lines. User-named markers are not offered (WP-19 timeline 2).

capabilities.capability: Sequencer: move and offset whole layers' animation blocks in time.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets an animator re-time whole performances without touching keys.

match.note: Clip layers move and resize, and line-relative times stay line-relative. Dragging shots and lines is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Push frames left or right: insert or remove time across all layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to open up a pause or cut frames late in production.

match.note: Changing a line's slot or voice re-flows shots, acting, captions and cues automatically. A direct insert-time edit is not offered.

capabilities.capability: Relative keyframing: offset a pose additively across existing keys.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets an animator adjust a whole range at once.

match.note: Additive clip layers add on top of the stack.

capabilities.capability: Mute or hide animation channels.
capabilities.pro_use: Isolates parts of the animation while polishing.

match.note: A clip layer's weight 0 mutes it. There is no per-joint channel mute.

capabilities.capability: Multiple layers shown together in the timeline, and playing a chosen segment.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to compare timing across characters.

match.note: The Studio timeline shows every character's lanes, the dialogue and the shots. shot.render renders one shot.

capabilities.capability: Audio recording inside the app, straight onto the timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for scratch dialogue for animatics and for solo creators' final voices.

match.note: Voices are synthesised and aligned. Human voice-over import with phone-level alignment, fitted to slots, is WP-13.

capabilities.capability: Actions window: named reusable animations (walk, wave, blink) stored with a rig and inserted on the timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Builds a motion library per character.

match.note: There are 33 library clips plus each character's own clips (v0.7). They are added with timeline.edit add_clip or from prose with acting.direct.

capabilities.capability: Blending actions onto the timeline with weights, and making actions relative.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets an animator layer a gesture over a walk.

match.note: A nonlinear clip stack with fades, weights, additive layers and base layers.

capabilities.capability: Export and import actions, including child layers (14.5), between files and rigs.
capabilities.pro_use: Shares motion across shows.

match.note: Clips are template-level, so they work across every character on a template. actout.clip retargets takes onto any rig.

capabilities.capability: Automatic lip sync: analyse an audio track to drive a mouth switch layer, with random alternate visemes (13.5.3), and label phonemes on the timeline (14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Cuts most of the lip-sync work in dialogue-heavy series.

match.note: Visemes come from the TTS phoneme timings or the aligner, are written to timing.json and drive the mouth swap. lipsync.check measures lag and correlation against the voice.

capabilities.capability: Smart Bone lip sync (14.5): phoneme poses that drive the whole face (jaw, cheeks) rather than only mouth drawings.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives richer, rig-driven dialogue acting.

match.note: Phoneme poses drive the whole face (lipsync: angles, shifts and scales per mouth shape, cross-faded with the visemes) besides the mouth drawings.

capabilities.capability: New document, new workspace and new from template.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives consistent project setups per show.

match.note: Format templates draft the script, shots and timing.

capabilities.capability: Gather media: copy every external file a project uses into its folder.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to archive and hand projects to other studios.

match.note: film.provenance lists what shaped a film, and export.web inlines everything for the player. A gathered hand-off package with stems is WP-22.

capabilities.capability: Save as older file versions and strip comments and tags.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to share with collaborators on older versions.

match.note: There is a single in-house format, versioned (puppet 'version'). Older files stay valid in newer loaders.

capabilities.capability: Project settings: size, frame rate (including 23.976), background, depth of field, 3D camera, stereo and noise grain.
capabilities.pro_use: Sets the delivery spec for a show.

match.note: The QA bar is fixed at 1080x1920 at 30 fps, and other aspects use film.render's 'aspect'. Grain is in the finishing presets. Depth of field is WP-36, and higher-frame-rate or 4K masters are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Import images, image sequences, movies, SVG, audio, OBJ models and other Moho documents.
capabilities.pro_use: Brings outside art, plates and assets into a scene.

match.note: Characters can come from SVG, PSD, ORA, photos and Blender rigs. Image sequences and movies as scene layers are WP-35 and WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Photoshop import with layers becoming separate parts (with clipping and blend modes, 14.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Brings illustrators' layered art into the rig.

match.note: Maps PSD layer names to template parts, swaps, pivots and anchors. PSD blend modes are not kept (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Real-time media connection: imported images update live when they are edited in another program.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets painters revise art while animators keep working.

match.note: There is a round trip by export and re-import, but no live link. Krita .kra import is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Preview renders and preview animations (lower quality, quick).
capabilities.pro_use: Used to check timing and look before a full render.

match.note: The animatic takes seconds, the player preview is live, and one shot can be rendered alone.

capabilities.capability: Export animation to video and image sequences: MP4 (H.264 default in 14.5, H.265), MOV ProRes with alpha, AVI, PNG/TIFF/WebP/PSD sequences, animated GIF and SVG sequences.
capabilities.pro_use: Delivers to editors, platforms and compositors.

match.note: film.render delivers H.264 per the platform profiles. WebM and ProRes with alpha, GIF and APNG are WP-23.

capabilities.capability: OpenEXR export and import with bit depth, colour spaces (including ACEScg) and compression (14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: High-precision frames for compositing and post.

match.note: EXR export in half float with ACEScg (OCIO); EXR import is WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Moho Exporter: a batch render queue in a separate process, with per-item status and reruns (14.5).
capabilities.pro_use: Renders a whole episode's scenes overnight.

match.note: Async jobs, incremental re-render by content hash, and parallel film sessions on the board already exist. Distributed render workers are WP-38.

capabilities.capability: Export to game engines and Blender (14.4): glTF/GLB with rig, actions and Smart Bones as morph targets; FBX for Unity.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets 2D characters run inside games and 3D pipelines.

match.note: Lottie (export.lottie) and Synfig (export.synfig) exist. Game runtime export (Godot, sprite sheets) is WP-30.

capabilities.capability: Export a single frame to SVG.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for print, marketing stills and vector hand-off.

match.note: Stills and model sheets exist (PNG, plus SVG from the Rig Canvas sheet). Print-ready transparent stills are WP-23.

capabilities.capability: Export the full soundtrack or a single audio layer as WAV.
capabilities.pro_use: Hands the mix to a sound editor.

match.note: Writes the mix and the voice, music and effects stems to build/. A stems hand-off to editors is WP-22.

capabilities.capability: Undo and redo history, with merged steps for repeated edits (14.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Lets artists experiment safely.

match.note: Films are text, so every version can be diffed and re-rendered exactly. The Studio timeline also has Ctrl+Z.

capabilities.capability: Copy and paste layers with their animation, and paste relative.
capabilities.pro_use: Reuses animation across scenes.

match.note: Clips and cast references are reused by name, and inserts come from other films in edit lists. A copy-paste of a timeline range is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Custom keyboard shortcuts and device presets.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives speed for power users.

match.note: Doodleberry is agent-native: commands are reached through the CLI, HTTP and MCP. Studio has a few fixed keys.

capabilities.capability: Preferences: tool defaults, input devices, autosave and display.
capabilities.pro_use: Sets per-artist and per-studio behaviour.

match.note: Environment variables pick binaries and quality, and profiles hold per-style QA thresholds and encoding.

capabilities.capability: Snap to grid.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for precise layouts and props.

match.note: The Rig Canvas has no grid. The Studio timeline snaps to frames and words.

capabilities.capability: Reset or randomise line widths, and peak or smooth selected points.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for quick line-quality passes.

match.note: Line-quality controls belong with line styles in WP-15. Point corner editing is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Raise or lower shapes, to front or back (stacking order within a layer), animatable.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to fix overlaps such as a hand behind a sleeve.

match.note: Z order is per part and per swap, and controls and clips can switch it over time.

capabilities.capability: Trace image: vectorise a bitmap automatically.
capabilities.pro_use: Turns sketches and scans into editable vectors.

match.note: Ink-fidelity import keeps scans as raster parts (puppet.from_ink). Vector tracing (VTracer, potrace) is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Create a mesh layer and triangulate a 2D mesh over artwork.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives smooth deformation of painted art.

match.note: Skinned mesh strokes exist (from Blender cut-out rigs), but there is no in-house triangulation of an arbitrary drawing.

capabilities.capability: Curver layers: bend artwork along an animatable spline, including compressible curvers.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for rubber-hose limbs, tails and bending props.

match.note: Bendy limbs curve parts at joints (SVG and Grease Pencil). Spline deformers on any layer are a WP-34 candidate.

capabilities.capability: Freeze points and reset points: key the current shape, or restore the rest shape.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to lock and unlock poses during animation.

match.note: Named poses are saved and keyed (poses: [[t, name]]). Point-level freezing does not apply, because shapes are not animated per point.

capabilities.capability: Smooth joint for a bone pair: an automatic curved elbow or knee.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives clean bends without corrective drawings.

match.note: 'bend': {'width'} curves a limb out of its parent while keeping its thickness. It works in SVG and Grease Pencil; Synfig and Lottie stay rigid (WP-14).

capabilities.capability: Release, flexi-bind and link bones to layers (re-binding art to the skeleton).
capabilities.pro_use: Used to fix and rework rigs.

match.note: Binding is implicit (art belongs to a part). Re-binding means editing the puppet or re-importing it. A Rig Canvas editing pass is WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Track a bone to video.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives motion capture of a single point onto a rig.

match.note: Body landmarks retarget to joint angles and root travel. Arbitrary point tracking is WP-12.

capabilities.capability: Make Smart Bone dial: build a control and its actions in one step.
capabilities.pro_use: Speeds up face and turn rigs.

match.note: Generated characters get a turn control. Authoring other controls is JSON only, with no canvas tool (WP-18).

capabilities.capability: Freeze pose, freeze selected bones, and reset bones.
capabilities.pro_use: Keys every bone at once to hold or restore a pose.

match.note: The Rig Canvas 'Key' and 'Save pose' record full poses.

capabilities.capability: Hide, shy or controlled bones, and coloured bones.
capabilities.pro_use: Declutters complex rigs.

match.note: This is display-only GUI management.

capabilities.capability: Bone dynamics: follow-through on rotation, scale and position with weight and gravity, delayed (lagging or leading) control bones (14.0), and toggling by Smart Bones (14.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Gives automatic overlap on hair, ears, tails and cloth.

match.note: Deterministic damped springs follow a driver part, and chains have a travelling wave. Parts have no gravity and no position or scale dynamics (WP-42); props do (physics.solve).

capabilities.capability: Set a layer's start time and offset its animation.
capabilities.pro_use: Staggers repeated characters or actions.

match.note: Any time can reference a line ('mid.start+0.9') or be given in seconds.

capabilities.capability: Rescale keyframes: stretch or compress the timing of a range.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for quick timing fixes.

match.note: resize_clip changes a clip layer's length, and the puppet's 'acting.tempo' scales a character's clip speed. Rescaling an arbitrary range of keys is not offered (WP-19 timeline 2).

capabilities.capability: Copy deep frame or frame range: copy every layer's state at a time and paste it elsewhere.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for holds and returns to a key pose.

match.note: Poses and clips can be re-added at any time. A range copy across all characters is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Nudge a physics object: give it an impulse at a frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Starts simulations on cue.

match.note: physics impulses {t, body, v} kick a body at a time; a prop's attach key starts a throw or drop.

capabilities.capability: Audio level, mute and restart of audio and movie tracks.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for a working mix while animating.

match.note: The mix is automatic (ducking, then -14 LUFS measured by qa.run). Manual per-cue levels in Studio are WP-40.

capabilities.capability: Align a layer with the camera (billboarding) and allow frame skipping during playback.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps flat cards facing a 3D camera, and gives real-time previews.

match.note: There is no 3D camera in the 2D path, and the preview plays the renderer directly.

capabilities.capability: Lua scripting API (Lua 5.4 in 14.0) for custom tools, menu commands and automation, with documentation.
capabilities.pro_use: Pipeline TDs automate rig building, batch fixes and studio tools.

match.note: Every feature is an @command with a JSON schema, reachable from the CLI, HTTP, MCP and Studio.

capabilities.capability: Embedded layer scripts that run every frame for procedural animation.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for procedural wiggles, clocks and data-driven motion.

match.note: Scene films are frame functions that must be pure functions of the frame number. Data-bound kit elements read data.json.

capabilities.capability: Bundled script packs: tiling, visibility, particle effects, layer effects, warp, sound and 3D helpers.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives ready-made effects without coding.

match.note: The explainer kit and motion effects cover some cases. Procedural tiling, scatter and particles are WP-42.

capabilities.capability: Installing third-party scripts.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets studios add community tools.

match.note: Third-party code is vendored with UPSTREAM.json, a licence class and a recorded build. A new command is added in dbe/commands.py.

capabilities.capability: Video safe zones and a rule-of-thirds overlay.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps titles and action inside the safe area for each platform.

match.note: Every visible word's box is measured against the platform-safe area per aspect. brand.assets writes the safe-area overlays. There is no rule-of-thirds guide.

capabilities.capability: Tracing image: a reference picture shown behind the canvas.
capabilities.pro_use: Used to draw over model sheets, sketches or photos.

match.note: Drawing requests give ghost guides (the character at rest, the related drawing, a target box). Arbitrary reference images in the Rig Canvas are WP-18.

capabilities.capability: Design mode: edit the rig without creating animation keys, then return to the main timeline.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeps rigging and animation separate.

match.note: The rig and the animation are separate files by design, so rig edits never create keys.

capabilities.capability: Stereo views (side by side, over-under, anaglyph) for 3D output.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for stereoscopic deliveries.

match.note: Stereo is outside the delivery targets (social video and web). Cinema-style packages are WP-37 if ever needed.

capabilities.capability: Grid display, curve display and fading unselected layers.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives drawing and editing clarity.

match.note: These are editor display aids. Grid snapping is tracked under moho-draw-menu-1.

capabilities.capability: Blend morphs window: mix several stored shape morphs with sliders.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for facial expressions and corrective shapes blended together.

match.note: There are no point morphs. Morphs between drawings and views are WP-43. Controls blend only angles, shifts, swaps and z.

capabilities.capability: Keyframe window: inspect and set a selected key's interpolation and its parameters.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives precise easing control.

match.note: Per-key interpolation editing comes with the curve editor in WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Switch selection window: choose which drawing a switch shows at the current frame.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for quick swap keying.

ref: acting timeline poses (mouth, eyes, brows, hand_R_pose)
match.note: Swap shapes are forced by name in poses and clips. acting.direct sets them from prose.

capabilities.capability: Docking layouts and toggling secondary windows.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets each artist arrange the workspace.

match.note: This is a GUI layout concern.

capabilities.capability: Manual, tutorials and video tutorials one click away.
capabilities.pro_use: Speeds up onboarding.

match.note: Commands list their own schemas. docs.check keeps the plan, feature map and registry in agreement.

capabilities.capability: Show autosave files for crash recovery.
capabilities.pro_use: Protects work after a crash.

match.note: There is no long-lived editor session to lose. Every edit is a file write through film.write or timeline.edit, kept in git.

capabilities.capability: Update checks, licence deactivation and refresh, the welcome screen, buying content, and About.
capabilities.pro_use: Handles product upkeep.

match.note: Doodleberry is in-house with no licensing or store.

capabilities.capability: Mesh warp (smart warp) layers: a triangulated mesh, posed by points or bones, bends any image or vector layer, and meshes can nest.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives organic squash, head turns and painted-art deformation.

match.note: Skinned mesh strokes deform raster textures by part weights (SVG only, WP-14). There is no animatable mesh-point warp on arbitrary layers (WP-34 deformers).

capabilities.capability: Quad and perspective warp (13.5): a four-point mesh puts flat art into true perspective.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for moving backgrounds, floors and signs in perspective.

match.note: 2D layers in depth are in the multiplane work, WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Frame-dependent warping: keyed changes to the warp mesh or curver over time.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for hand-tuned squash and stretch on specific frames.

match.note: Keyed per-part squash and stretch (timeline scales) and whole-body squash exist; general warp-mesh animation is WP-34.

capabilities.capability: Warp animation exported as morph targets to game engines (14.4).
capabilities.pro_use: Lets deformed 2D characters play in real-time engines.

match.note: Game export is in WP-30.

capabilities.capability: Edition tiers (Pro vs Debut) that cap frame count, resolution, Smart Bones, audio tracks and scripting.
capabilities.pro_use: Studios buy Pro for unlimited length and resolution.

match.note: There are no editions. The individual Pro features are mapped in the chapters above.

capabilities.capability: Vendor technical support channels.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets studios escalate blocking bugs.

match.note: Doodleberry is in-house R&D, so its maintainers are the support.

capabilities.capability: Attribution of third-party libraries and content providers.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives licence compliance for the tool and its bundled content.

match.note: Every component has a licence class. Credits are generated from what a film actually uses.

capabilities.capability: A keyboard shortcut reference, including keyframe navigation keys.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives speed for experienced artists.

match.note: Doodleberry is agent-native. The Studio timeline's few keys (space, arrows, Delete, Ctrl+Z) are documented in docs/dbe.md.

capabilities.capability: Supported import and export media, plus writing your own export presets.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets studios standardise delivery settings per client.

match.note: Per-platform encoding profiles (H.264 CRF 18, AAC 48 kHz, faststart, size caps) are used by film.package. More formats are WP-23.

chapters.chapter: Appendix F: Moho Document File Format

capabilities.capability: A documented, text-based project format (structure and tips) that tools can read and write.
capabilities.pro_use: Lets pipeline TDs generate and patch scenes outside the app.

match.note: Puppets and films are JSON with a published format and schemas. They are checked by film.validate on film.write and before every render.

capabilities.capability: Headless command-line rendering: format, codec preset, output path and frame range.
capabilities.pro_use: Used for render farms and scripted batch output.

match.note: Both run headless through python -m dbe. The renderer can be overridden per shot.

capabilities.capability: Command-line quality toggles (half size, half fps, effects off, fewer particles, antialiasing, premultiply) and layer-comp renders with suffixes or folders.
capabilities.pro_use: Gives fast previews and render passes from scripts.

match.note: Draft output comes from the animatic, and per-renderer outputs are written side by side. Named passes are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Logging, verbose time estimates, and Lua startup scripts from the command line (14.2).
capabilities.pro_use: Gives unattended automation with monitoring.

match.note: Any command runs from the CLI, with async jobs over HTTP. A cost and time estimate before rendering, plus progress events, is WP-20.
